title: Stage 0 — Onboarding
goal: Enter a working engineering environment and ship your first commit.
summary: Set up GitHub, your tools, and your project repo. Ship a real first commit.

checkpoint.prompt: Which command prints the installed Git version?
checkpoint.explanation: `git --version` prints the installed version. If it errors, Git is not installed yet.

checkpoint.prompt: Why does Git need your name and email?

choices.text: To stamp every commit with an author
To log you into GitHub automatically
To encrypt your repository

checkpoint.explanation: Git records the configured name/email as the author of each commit. It is identity metadata, not authentication.

checkpoint.prompt: After staging a file, which command saves it as a snapshot with a message?
checkpoint.explanation: `git commit -m "..."` records a snapshot of the staged changes with a message describing them.

choices.text: Uploads your local commits to the remote on GitHub
Saves your changes locally
Downloads the latest code from GitHub

checkpoint.explanation: `git push` sends commits that exist locally up to the remote. `git pull` is the download direction; `git commit` saves locally.

checkpoint.prompt: Why must you link your GitHub repository in the CommitLoop dashboard?

choices.text: So CommitLoop can read your real commit history as proof of work
So Git installs automatically on your machine
So the database creates tables for you

checkpoint.explanation: CommitLoop tracks progress from your GitHub repo. Linking connects your commits to your account.

checklist.label: GitHub repository created for your project
README describes your project domain in your own words
Repository linked in your CommitLoop dashboard

questions.prompt: What is the source of truth for your progress on CommitLoop?

choices.text: Your GitHub repository commits
Time spent watching lesson videos
Self-reported checkboxes only

questions.explanation: CommitLoop reads your real repo activity. Commits are the receipt — not intentions or watch time.

questions.prompt: How many project repositories do you maintain for a single track?

choices.text: One — it evolves for the whole track, no resets
A brand-new repo for every stage
As many throwaway clones as you like

questions.explanation: One repository grows across the entire track. Refactors and migrations are progress, not restarts.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between Git and GitHub?

choices.text: Git is the version-control tool on your machine; GitHub hosts repositories online
They are two names for the same program
Git is a website; GitHub is a desktop app

questions.explanation: Git runs locally and tracks history. GitHub is a hosting service for Git repositories plus collaboration features.

questions.prompt: You changed CSS but the page still looks wrong. Which tool do you open first?

choices.text: Chrome DevTools — Elements panel to inspect and live-edit styles
Postman — to send HTTP requests
DB Browser — to run SELECT queries

questions.explanation: DevTools Elements is for frontend structure and CSS. Postman and DB tools are for API and database layers.

questions.prompt: In Track 1's stack, how does the frontend get workout data from storage?

choices.text: Browser calls the Express API over HTTP; the API reads the database
JavaScript opens the SQLite file directly in the browser
GitHub stores the rows and serves them to HTML

questions.explanation: The frontend talks HTTP to the API; the API owns database access. Layers stay separated.
